new.n: War of 1812 money buried by a boiling spring, Delaney homestead, Coldwater Twp
new.pl: Edward Delaney homestead, sec. 22 T16N R6W, Coldwater Twp, Isabella Co.
new.st: The 1884 Isabella county album says the farm of Civil War veteran Edward Delaney (b. 1837 Rochester NY), sec 22, in Coldwater Twp held a boiling spring (~500 gal/min) venerated by the Ojibwe as an ancient burial place of their chiefs, and that "several individuals claim that in its immediate vicinity a large sum of money was buried during the second war with Great Britain". Copper was reported in the spring. His father-in-law William F. Baker (d. 1876) is buried on the farm. Pin is the section centre (about 800 m); the spring is not yet placed within the section.
new.t: Find the 80 acres within sec 22 on a 1879-1900 Isabella plat or the GLO homestead entry, then find the spring on LiDAR or the 1938 aerial. The spring area is a reputed Indian burial place and there is a family grave on the farm: LOOK-ONLY there; search only the wider vicinity with permission. Access: private; burial ground and family grave look-only.
src: Portrait and Biographical Album of Isabella County, Mich. (Chapman Bros., 1884), Coldwater Twp sketch of Delaney (archive.org portraitbiograph00ch)
new.warn: Reputed Ojibwe burial place at the spring and a family grave on the farm: look only there.
new.pinev: Edward Delaney residence sec 22 T16N R6W (1884 album); pin = section centre (BLM PLSS), ~800 m; 80-acre homestead filed 1867, "the first homesteaded north of the Indian reserve"; spring not yet placed within the section

set.pinev: 1905 Polk atlas of Brown Co., Sigel Twp: "Fred. Kuehn 160" in sec. 22; SW1/4 sec. 22 T109N R31W, quarter centre from BLM PLSS (about 400 m)

tw-mn-sigel-kuehn-plum-trees-1906.st: Placed from the 1905 Brown County atlas (Sigel Twp map): Fred. Kuehn held 160 acres in sec. 22, most likely the SW quarter of sec. 22 T109N R31W; the pin is that quarter's centre, good to about 400 m. Neighbours were Anton Baumann (sec. 21), Thos. Forstner, Hubert Hillesheim and Otto Schultz; John Kuehn had 131 acres on the west shore of School Lake in sec. 16.
